abstract: NOD-like receptors (NLRs) are intracellular immune sensors that monitor for pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs, DAMPs) and initiate innate immune signaling pathways upon detection. Dysregulation of NLR signaling contributes to numerous inflammatory diseases and cancers, yet mechanistic studies of NLR proteins are limited by the availability of reliable detection reagents, particularly in emerging model organisms such as zebrafish (Danio rerio). Although zebrafish provide a powerful system for studying innate immunity, few validated antibodies exist for zebrafish NLR proteins. Here, we describe the development of aptamer-based detection reagents targeting zebrafish NLRs using the APT-SNAP platform, a high-density aptamer microarray technology that enables rapid identification of protein-binding nucleic acid ligands. Using this approach, we identified multiple DNA aptamers that bind zebrafish NLR proteins and selected candidates targeting NOD2 for further characterization. Orthogonal validation assays, which include enzyme-linked apta-sorbent assays (ELASAs), pull-downs, biolayer interferometry (BLI), and fluorescence microscopy, confirmed that the lead aptamers bind zebrafish NOD2 with high affinity and specificity, and function effectively in biochemical and cellular assays. These results demonstrate that APT-SNAP generated validated, native-state affinity reagents for a zebrafish immune protein where commercial antibodies failed, providing new molecular tools for investigating NLR biology in zebrafish. More broadly, this strategy establishes a generalizable approach for generating affinity reagents against challenging protein targets that lack reliable antibodies.
